source.title: Emergence of Phonemic, Syntactic, and Semantic Representations in Artificial Neural Networks
source.authors: P. Orhan; Pablo J. Diego-Sim'on; Emmnanuel Chemla; Yair Lakretz; Yves Boubenec; Jean-Rémi King

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: Supplementary single-unit analyses report that semantic and syntactic coding is largely distributed across units, with some syntax-coding units standing out. This bears indirectly on the general neuron-as-analysis-unit premise, but the paper does not measure neuron poles, job counts, explanation accuracy, or attribution graphs as specified by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's main structural-probe results concern phonemic, lexical-semantic, and syntactic representations, not neuron job explanations, so they are not rows. The supplementary single-unit analyses are included because they measure unit contributions to those subspaces. The paper does not test any version as specifically stated.
record.test_reason: The paper fits linear structural probes for phonemic, lexical-semantic and syntactic distance in wav2vec 2.0, Pythia and Llama2 models. Its supplementary single-unit analyses of Llama2-13B ask how probe subspaces load on units. It never assigns jobs to neurons or neuron poles, never counts how many neurons are interpretable, and never scores explanations by activating examples or by simulation. It builds no attribution graphs and does not study InceptionV1. It neither tests nor relies on any version, and it does not cite the essay or the automated-explanation paper. The record's 'tests'/T5 classification is wrong: distributed probe loadings are a related but different construct and belong under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct for the supplementary unit analyses: semantic structure is distributed, and syntax is distributed with a few syntax-specialized units. The paper's main conclusion, however, is that speech and text models successively build phonemic, lexical and syntactic subspaces during training. These subspaces need 2–4 orders of magnitude more data than children receive.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses linear structural probes and regression from subspace activity to unit responses, rather than pole-level job explanations or attribution graphs.
record.method_sensitivity: The single-unit analyses are restricted to selected Llama2-13B layers with strong semantic and syntactic probe scores; the unit-response analysis uses a podcast transcript.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama2-13B, semantic and syntactic probe subspaces are nearly orthogonal (alignment about 0.04). Probe weights spread across all units, with 40–90 outlier units per layer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linearly probed linguistic structures in LLMs are carried by distributed, mutually unaligned patterns over neurons rather than by dedicated neurons.

fits_no_version.finding: A few units (36 in layer 15) are well predicted by syntactic-subspace activity (R² > 0.6), beyond what POS and dependency one-hot features explain. Inspecting their mean response by POS and dependency category gave no clear tuning explanation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some LLM neurons specialize in tree-distance syntax coding that simple categorical labels do not describe.

fits_no_version.finding: Semantic-subspace activity alone does not predict a large share of variance in any single unit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Lexical-semantic hierarchy is encoded fully distributed across units in Llama2-13B.

record.problems: The single-unit results are supplementary analyses of one Llama2-13B model. Probe weights were not regularized, and the paper notes this could have affected sparsity. Several reported unit-analysis outcomes are qualitative or lack numeric effect sizes.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were omitted under the row cap. The paper's main phonemic, semantic, and syntactic probing results were left out because they do not measure neuron-job explanations or unit-level contributions.

untested.parts: All: no audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or of one-job/two-job/unexplained shares.
All: no neuron-job shares in any model family, and no scaling to MoE or trillion-parameter models.
All: no InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neurons, and no test of superposition versus recursive generalization.
All: no comparison of architecture, regularization or tools against interpretable-neuron share.
All: no attribution graphs and no replacement-model comparison.
All: no explanation fitted to activating examples is tested for predicting firing. The by-eye check of syntax units' POS tuning is not an explanation-versus-prediction test.
All: no simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: Off-topic for this phenomenon: a structural-probing and language-acquisition paper. The only point of contact is the supplementary unit analysis. Its by-eye finding that syntax units lacked an obvious POS tuning is loosely related to V6 but is not a test of it.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit Qwen3-32B poles, assign named jobs, or report the claimed one-job/two-job/ununderstood shares.
Does not measure neuron-job shares across model families or scale to trillions of parameters.
Does not analyze InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons or test recursive generalization against superposition.
Does not compare architecture, regularization, or tools for neuron interpretability, or estimate interpretable-neuron shares in vision models.
Does not construct attribution graphs or test whether they explain model behavior without a replacement model.
Does not test explanations against new activating examples or measure where a neuron fires.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: Llama2-13B
rows.operation_detail: Measured alignment between semantic and syntactic probe subspaces using mean squared cosines of principal angles.

conditions.value: 34 of 40 layers selected for semantic and syntactic scores above 80% of their respective maxima

rows.measure: Subspace alignment; 0 denotes orthogonal subspaces and 1 perfectly aligned subspaces.
rows.locator: Appendix, Single unit analyses; Supplementary Figure H, panel A
rows.note: The authors interpret these values as indicating that the two subspaces are mostly unaligned; this is not a measurement of neuron-job explanations.
rows.check: This is a probe-subspace alignment score, not a measure of individual neurons' jobs. Keeping it as context is fine, but it bears on no version.

rows.subject: Llama2-13B
rows.operation_detail: Measured each unit's norm in the semantic and syntactic probe vectors and identified outliers.

conditions.value: layers with semantic and syntactic scores above 80% of their respective maxima

rows.measure: Distribution and counts of units with outlier probe-weight norms.
rows.value: Probe weights were spread across all units; 40 to 90 units, depending on the layer, had outlier norms ranging from 2 to 3 times the median; at most 20 units were outliers for both subspaces.
rows.locator: Appendix, Single unit analyses; Supplementary Figure H, panels B-C
rows.note: The paper says probe norms were not explicitly regularized, which could have favored a sparser solution. It reports that the number of units that were outliers for both subspaces increased across layers.
rows.check: These are probe-weight norms per unit. The probes are unregularized, so the norms say nothing about whether a neuron has one main job.

rows.subject: Llama2-13B
rows.operation_detail: Used ridge regression to predict individual unit responses from semantic and syntactic subspace activity.

conditions.value: 5 outer and 5 inner sequential-block cross-validation folds

rows.measure: Number of units whose response variance was strongly predicted by syntactic subspace activity.
rows.locator: Appendix, Single unit analyses; Supplementary Figure H, panel D
rows.note: The authors report that these units matched outlier units from the probe-weight analysis.
rows.check: Unit responses are predicted from probe subspaces; no neuron explanation is scored. The 34-of-40 layer selection applies to this encoding analysis, but the value reported is for layer 15 only.

rows.subject: Llama2-13B
rows.operation_detail: Compared unit-response variance explained by univariate syntactic features alone with variance explained by those features plus subspace activity.
rows.measure: Change in variance explained for individual unit responses.
rows.baseline: Regression using univariate syntactic features alone
rows.value: Adding syntactic subspace activity strongly increased the variance explained, including for outlier units.
rows.locator: Appendix, Single unit analyses; Supplementary Figure H, panel E
rows.note: No numeric change in variance explained is stated in the text.
rows.check: No numeric value is given in the text (Fig. H, panel E only). This is not a neuron-explanation measure.

rows.subject: Llama2-13B
rows.operation_detail: Tested whether semantic subspace activity predicted individual unit responses in the encoding analysis.

conditions.value: layers selected for strong semantic and syntactic scores

rows.measure: Whether semantic subspace activity alone predicted a large share of any individual unit's response variance.
rows.value: No such effect was observed: semantic subspace activity was not sufficient by itself to predict a large variance of any single unit response.
rows.note: The authors contrast this with the syntax-subspace result; no numerical threshold for “large” is given.
rows.check: This is a qualitative null with no threshold, and it is not a neuron-job measure.

rows.subject: Llama2-13B
rows.operation_detail: Measured correlations between the responses of the syntax-associated units across words in the podcast dataset.

conditions.value: Units identified in the syntax analysis

rows.value: mean correlation: 0.002; max across two units: 0.39
rows.note: The authors cite these values as evidence that the units had distinct roles in encoding syntactic information.
rows.check: This is a response correlation among syntax-linked units, not a measure of interpretability share.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
